hard_rules: The final player guide must be understandable by a new player and executable step by step.
Every task block must include exact start point, travel method, accepted quests, objective order, turn-ins, five-box interaction mode, expected XP, expected minutes, and stop-loss conditions.
Do not call a route fastest unless alternatives have been compared using the same cost model.
Do not full-clear a zone merely because quests exist there.
Personal high-count random drops are skipped by default unless mandatory or overlapping with multiple high-value tasks.
Shared kills, fixed objects, named targets, and route-overlapping travel quests receive priority.

Main-character control is not itself a penalty: riding, combat, a short jump, one spell/item use, or brief manual pathing are baseline control costs. Only incremental time beyond normal play is charged.

Five-box interaction cost must distinguish baseline main-character control, brief main-character path deviation, per-character serial switching, and formation-breaking operations such as follower loss, repeated positioning, respawn waiting, or failure retries.
A short main-character-only terrain action can be highly efficient when followers remain in range or complete automatically; do not penalize it merely because it requires manual execution.

The guaranteed route must not require auction-house purchases, mailed materials, crafted items, or meaningful upfront gold. Already-owned materials may unlock optional bonus branches but cannot be counted in guaranteed XP.

Single-character leveling videos are feasibility and location evidence only. They may prove quest order, entrances, dense spawn areas, mechanics, and practical task blocks, but they do not define the five-box candidate set, optimal zone order, or expected completion time.

The five-box optimizer must search the full Horde quest candidate pool independently of the video route. A task omitted by the video can still be optimal for five-box play because full quest XP is awarded to every character while shared kills are completed once for the party.

Corpse-use and scene-object tasks are not assumed to require simultaneous interaction. Treat them as group-shared when one use advances the party, otherwise as short sequential interactions; an in-use lock or normal respawn is not by itself a rejection reason.
Travel time includes riding, flight, ship, zeppelin, waiting, vertical navigation, and return visits, but only actual incremental minutes are charged.
Drop-rate estimates must be marked as assumptions until replaced by server-specific observations.
All deferred tasks must have a named future revisit trigger; otherwise they are classified as skipped.
The previous 35-to-43 full-clear draft is not evidence of fastest routing.
